clips.text_zh: WHERE IS THE MONEY GOING? GOLD crashing. SILVER crashing. STOCKS crashing. BITCOIN crashing. The fuck is going on!!! 靠，咁樣真係唔知邊度先搵到錢。
clips.text_en_b1: Where is the money going? Gold is crashing. Silver is crashing. Stocks are crashing. Bitcoin is crashing. The fuck is going on?! Every major market is falling, and nobody seems to know where the money is going.
clips.text_en_b2: Where is all the money going? Gold is crashing, silver is crashing, stocks are crashing, and Bitcoin is falling as well. What the hell is going on?! It feels as though every major market has entered free fall at the same time, although nobody appears to have a clear explanation. Everyone is searching for somewhere to put their cash, yet investors are clearly getting cold feet.
clips.text_en_c1: Where is the money going? Gold is crashing, silver is crashing, stocks are crashing, and Bitcoin is crashing. What the fuck is going on?! Every major market appears to be falling at once, yet nobody seems able to identify where the money is heading. One minute, these assets are being treated as safe havens or speculative bets; the next, they are all sliding together. If this is a coordinated sell-off, the trigger must be something significant. Otherwise, it looks less like a normal correction and more like broad panic sweeping across every corner of the market.
clips.text_en_c2: Where on earth is the money going? Gold is crashing. Silver is crashing. Stocks are crashing. Bitcoin is crashing. What the hell is going on?! Every major market appears to be selling off in unison, yet nobody seems able to identify where the capital is fleeing. Is it leaving equities for cash, rotating between assets, or simply being liquidated to cover losses elsewhere? The synchronised collapse is precisely what makes the panic so difficult to explain: there is no obvious safe harbour, no single culprit, and no coherent explanation. Everyone is running for the exits at once, and the money may be going nowhere in particular, which is arguably worse.
clips.source_hint: An anon panics as gold, silver, stocks, and Bitcoin fall together.

clips.text_en_b1: You guys told me to buy silver at 93 dollars. You said it was the new crypto. I fucking hate you guys. Nobody should take advice from this retarded board. Silver was supposed to be the next big trade, but now it is just another expensive lesson.
clips.text_en_b2: You people told me to buy silver at 93 dollars, and you also claimed it was the new crypto. I fucking hate all of you. Nobody should take financial advice from this retarded board. Silver was supposed to be the next big trade, but instead it has become another expensive lesson. Apparently, jumping on the hype was a brilliant idea, so congratulations on turning my savings into tuition.
clips.text_en_c1: You guys told me to buy silver at 93 dollars. You said it was the new crypto, the next explosive trade, and I fucking hate you for it. Nobody should take financial advice from this retarded board, especially when the promised revolution turns into another spectacularly expensive lesson. Silver was supposed to become the next big investment, but now it is simply tuition paid in the form of losses. If the market was going to replace Bitcoin, perhaps the least it could have done was tell us before the price collapsed. I should have ignored the hype and trusted my own judgment.
clips.text_en_c2: You people told me to buy silver at 93 dollars. You insisted it was the new crypto, the inevitable successor to every asset that had already made you rich. I fucking hate you lot. Nobody should take financial advice from this retarded board, which treats every market like a casino and every losing position as someone else’s fault. Silver was supposed to be the next great trade, a tidy little thesis that was supposed to print money. Instead, it has become another exorbitant lesson in market timing, speculative overreach, and the damage wrought when a crowd confuses enthusiasm with analysis. Ninety-three dollars, and I am the one paying for the lesson.
clips.source_hint: An anon says board advice turned a silver purchase into another costly lesson.

I know friends in accounting, marketing, and other bullshit jobs who now just give their tasks to Claude and send the result back. Claude hallucinates less than humans typo or make stuff up, so it is a better employee than most employees. And this did not suddenly change with Opus 5.5. It was already partly true before. Yet there is no visible unemployment spiral. 靠AI續命，連accounting都可能冇得做。
clips.text_en_b1: I’m freaking out about this conspiracy. Opus 5.5 can and has been able to do about 90% of office work. Friends in accounting and marketing now give tasks to Claude and send the results back. Claude makes fewer mistakes than many employees, yet there is still no visible unemployment spiral.
clips.text_en_b2: I’m freaking out about this conspiracy. Opus 5.5 can, and has been able to, handle roughly 90% of ordinary office work. I know people in accounting, marketing, and other bullshit jobs who now assign their tasks to Claude and send the results straight back. Claude hallucinates less often than many employees typo or invent things, so it is arguably a better worker than most. This did not suddenly begin with Opus 5.5; it was already partly true before.
clips.text_en_c1: I’m freaking out about this conspiracy because Opus 5.5 can, and has long been able to, perform roughly 90% of all office work. I know friends in accounting, marketing, and a range of other bullshit jobs who now hand their tasks to Claude and simply send the results back as if a human produced them. Claude hallucinates less frequently than many employees make typos, invent facts, or misunderstand instructions, which makes it a better employee than most. What troubles me is that this did not suddenly begin with Opus 5.5; it was already partly true beforehand. Yet there is still no visible unemployment spiral.
clips.text_en_c2: I am freaking out about this conspiracy, because the evidence is rather less speculative than I would like. Claude Opus 5.5 can, and has for some time been able to, carry out roughly 90% of ordinary office work. I know people in accounting, marketing, and other bullshit jobs who now delegate their assignments to Claude and pass the output off as their own. What makes this especially awkward is that the model hallucinates less often than many employees make typos, invent facts, or simply produce competent-looking nonsense. Crucially, none of this appeared suddenly with Opus 5.5; it was already partly true beforehand. Yet there is still no visible unemployment spiral, which is either reassuring or deeply suspicious, depending on how generously one interprets the labour market.
clips.source_hint: The OP claims Claude already handles most office work without visible unemployment rising.

clips.text_en_b1: China won. The post is basically just that statement, followed by a link to a Proud Socialist post on X. There is no detailed argument here, just a very confident conclusion and a link for the discussion to continue.
clips.text_en_b2: China won. The post consists of little more than that statement, followed by a link to a Proud Socialist post on X. There is no detailed argument, no supporting evidence, and no explanation of what exactly China has supposedly achieved. It is simply a very confident conclusion, although the link leaves the discussion open for everyone else to continue, interpret, and probably argue about.
clips.text_en_c1: China won. That is the entire post: a bold, emphatic statement followed by a link to a Proud Socialist post on X. There is no detailed argument, supporting evidence, explanation, or even a clearly defined claim about what exactly China has won. Instead, the thread relies on absolute confidence and invites the discussion to continue elsewhere. The post is so sparse that interpretation depends entirely on the linked material. Whether the confidence is justified is therefore impossible to assess from the original text alone; anyone wishing to understand the intended meaning would have to open the link and examine the broader political context surrounding it.
clips.text_en_c2: China won. The post consists, in essence, of that declaration, followed by a link to a Proud Socialist post on X. There is no elaborate argument, no supporting evidence, no breakdown of policy, no discussion of economic data, and no attempt to explain precisely what “won” is supposed to mean. It is simply a very confident conclusion, delivered with the ceremonial certainty of a victory announcement, after which the link invites discussion to continue elsewhere. The original Chinese comment observes that Hong Kong is so crowded that people have hardly any room to live, then asks the obvious question: if China has won, what exactly has been won, and for whom? For the moment, however, nuance is conspicuously absent.
clips.source_hint: A minimal post declares that China won and links an X post.

clips.text_zh: Low bar squat is genuinely one of the worst exercises ever popularized. It mostly just fries your CNS while barely even training the quads. The movement becomes a posterior-dominant hip and glute hinge as soon as the bar drops an inch lower. Quads get almost nothing, depth is usually garbage, and mainly fat powerlifters defend it because they can move more weight by turning a squat into a good morning. 結構上 load path 都變咗，唔係越深越好。
clips.text_en_b1: Low bar squats are among the worst exercises ever popularized. They mostly fry the CNS while barely training the quads. The movement becomes a posterior-dominant hip and glute hinge when the bar drops lower. Depth is usually bad, but some powerlifters defend it because they can move more weight.
clips.text_en_b2: Low bar squats are genuinely among the worst exercises ever popularized. They mainly tax the central nervous system while barely training the quadriceps. Once the bar drops even slightly lower, the movement turns into a posterior-dominant hinge through the hips and glutes. The quads receive almost nothing, depth is usually terrible, and mainly overweight powerlifters defend it because they can move more weight by turning a squat into a good morning.
clips.text_en_c1: The low-bar squat is genuinely one of the worst exercises ever popularized. Rather than delivering meaningful quad stimulation, it mostly fries the central nervous system and turns the movement into a posterior-dominant hip-and-glute hinge as soon as the bar drops even slightly lower. Depth is usually rubbish, yet some fat powerlifters defend the variation because they can move more weight by effectively turning a squat into a good morning. If the load path shifts toward the hips and glutes, then simply sinking lower does not automatically make the exercise better. In this case, increased depth may reduce its usefulness instead of improving it.
clips.text_en_c2: The low-bar squat is genuinely one of the worst exercises ever to have been popularised. For most lifters, it wrecks the central nervous system while doing little to develop the quadriceps, the muscle group it is conventionally assumed to train. Lower the bar even slightly and the movement becomes a posterior-dominant hinge: the hips and glutes take over, the torso folds forward, and the quads receive comparatively little stimulation. Depth is usually rubbish as well, since the range of motion ends once the lifter can no longer preserve a sensible spinal position. Fat powerlifters tend to defend the exercise because they can move heavier loads by converting a squat into a good morning with a barbell, but added weight is not synonymous with a better exercise.
clips.source_hint: The OP argues that low bar squats use a bad movement pattern and train quads poorly.
